po.identificationDescLocked: Supplier is locked once lines exist — clear the lines first if you need to change it.
po.identificationDesc: Which supplier this PO is being placed with.
po.noActiveSuppliers: No active suppliers. Add one in Suppliers first.
po.datesDesc: Order date is mandatory; expected date is advisory and used for the dashboard 'arriving soon' view.
po.billingDesc: The total currency drives the PO's summed total. Individual lines can still be quoted in other currencies — those are converted to DKK via the per-line FX rate.
po.notesDesc: Internal — e.g. reference numbers, freight instructions, who at the supplier confirmed.
po.notesPlaceholder: Free text. Cancellations append themselves here automatically.

poDetail.emailDesc: Sends the order document (same content as the print view) to {supplier}'s email on file. PO and line notes stay internal — only the message below reaches them.
poDetail.testModeBanner: Outbound test mode is on — this email goes to <mono>{recipients}</mono> instead of the supplier. Turn it off under Admin → Settings → Communication to go live.
poDetail.messagePlaceholder: e.g. Please confirm prices and delivery week.
poDetail.cancelDesc: The PO will be cancelled and the reason will be appended to its notes for the audit trail. Already-received stock movements are unaffected.
poDetail.cancelReasonPlaceholder: e.g. Supplier confirmed back-order pushes delivery past the project deadline.
poDetail.descDraft: Editable while draft. Once you move the PO to placed, lines lock and only the receive flow can change them.
poDetail.descCancelled: This PO is cancelled — lines are read-only.
poDetail.descReceived: This PO is fully received — lines are read-only.
poDetail.descLocked: Lines are locked. Use the receive flow below to log incoming stock.
poDetail.noLinesDraft: No lines yet — add the first one to get started.
poDetail.dialogDesc: Landed DKK/unit = unit price × FX rate × (1 + transport % + import duty %). Both percentages are frozen onto this line at insert; later admin edits don't retroactively change cost basis.
poDetail.filterPartsPlaceholder: Filter parts by SKU or name…
poDetail.unitPriceHint: Leave blank if the supplier hasn't quoted yet — fill it in from the order confirmation before receiving.
poDetail.fxOverrideHint: . Override if your invoice quotes a different rate.
poDetail.fxPrefilled: Pre-filled from the latest fx_rates row. Override if you have a fresher number on the invoice.
poDetail.fxNoRate: No FX rate on file for {currency} — enter manually.
poDetail.transportHint: Freight markup as a percent — e.g. 10 for 10 %. Default from /admin/settings.
poDetail.importHintPrepaid: Import duty prepaid by the supplier.
poDetail.importHintUnclassified: Origin unclassified — import tax off by default. Set the origin on the part.
poDetail.importHintSuffix: Override for this line by toggling; the choice and its reason are frozen onto the line.
poDetail.importHintNoPart: Pick a part — the default follows its origin and the supplier's duty-prepaid setting.
poDetail.lineNotesPlaceholder: Optional — e.g. supplier SKU on this PO, packing details.
poDetail.receiveErrNoQtys: No quantities entered. Type how many units arrived.
poDetail.recorded: {count, plural, one {Recorded 1 line receipt.} other {Recorded # line receipts.}}
poDetail.receiveDesc: Enter how many units arrived in this delivery. The DKK landed cost from the order is used for inventory valuation.

so.title: Sales orders
so.subtitle: Customer commitments. A confirmed SO slates bikes in linked MOs to the customer; delivery flips them to assigned.
so.emptyDesc: Create a sales order to quote, build, and deliver bikes for a customer.
so.newSubtitle: Create a draft. You'll add lines and spawn MOs from the detail page after.
so.editSubtitle: Header is editable while draft. Lines + status moves live on the detail page.
so.notesPlaceholder: Internal notes — not on the customer-facing documents.
so.cancelDesc: The SO will be cancelled and any unbuilt bikes linked to it get unslated (their owner pointer cleared). Built bikes stay slated — the workshop unpacks the orphan by hand. The reason is appended to the SO notes for the audit trail.
so.cancelReasonPlaceholder: e.g. Customer cancelled the order before any bikes were built.

soDetail.linkedMosDesc: MOs spawned from this SO's bike-template lines. Open each to follow build progress.
soDetail.noMos: No MOs yet — spawn one from a template line above.
soDetail.linkedPaintDesc: Paint batches created from this SO's frames. A frame at the painter can't be built until it's received back.
soDetail.noPaintOrdersCta: — send a batch of frames to the painter above.
soDetail.paymentsDesc: Deposits and the final invoice for this order. Down payments are taken before delivery; the final bills the remaining balance.
soDetail.noInvoicesCta: — take a deposit above, or invoice in full at delivery.
soDetail.productionNotePlaceholder: Labeling / production instructions for the build floor — e.g. apply Copenhagen kommune asset stickers, fleet numbers 100–150.
soDetail.noProductionNote: No labeling note. Add one so the build floor sees it on every bike.
soDetail.linesDescEditable: Editable while draft. Lines lock when the SO is confirmed.
soDetail.linesDescLocked: Lines are locked — the SO is past draft.
soDetail.noLinesEditable: No lines yet — add the first one to get started.
soDetail.lineDialogDesc: Bike templates spawn an MO when the SO is confirmed; parts are priced on the invoice but don't trigger production.
soDetail.descEnPlaceholder: Override or extend the catalog description.
soDetail.pickPrepayParts: Pick the parts the customer is paying for up front (e.g. the frames).
soDetail.exceedsRemaining: Exceeds the {remaining} still un-deposited on this order.
soDetail.newDepositSubtitle: A down payment on <mono>{so}</mono>, taken before delivery. VAT is recognised when you issue it. The final invoice will bill only the remaining balance.
soDetail.depositNoValue: This order has no value to take a deposit on — add priced lines first.
soDetail.depositWrongStatus: Deposits can be taken on a confirmed–ready order. This one is {status}.
soDetail.paintFramesSubtitle: Pick the frames to send to the painter as one batch. The paint order links back to this sales order.
soDetail.cantPaintDesc: Paint orders are part of the build pipeline, so they can only be created while the SO is still in production.
soDetail.errPickFrame: Pick at least one frame to paint.
soDetail.noFramesDesc: Every bike on {so} is either already in an open paint order or this SO has no bikes yet. Spawn an MO and add bikes first.
soDetail.framesSelected: {selected} of {total} selected. Only frames not already in an open paint order are shown.
soDetail.painterColourDesc: Frame + fork item lines are seeded automatically in this colour, one per selected frame — adjust them or add mudguards, signs and carriers on the order page. Prices come from the painter's price list.
soDetail.scheduleDesc: Advisory only; actual sent / received timestamps are stamped on status transitions.
soDetail.createPaintOrder: {count, plural, one {Create paint order (1 frame)} other {Create paint order (# frames)}}

paintOrders.title: Paint orders
paintOrders.noMatchFilter: No paint orders match this status filter.
paintOrders.emptyDesc: Paint orders are batches of bikes sent to a supplier for paint.
paintOrders.newSubtitle: One round trip with the painter. Add the item lines (what gets painted) and the bikes that ship with the batch on the next screen.
paintOrders.whoWhatDesc: Pick the painter (typically Metacoat A/S). The colour is an optional batch default — it pre-fills the item lines you add on the next screen, where the pricing comes from the painter's price list.
paintOrders.batchColourPlaceholder: No default — set per item line
paintOrders.scheduleDesc: Advisory only; actual sent / received timestamps are stamped on status transitions. Cost is per item line, frozen from the price list when the order is sent.

paintOrderDetail.cancelDesc: The order will be cancelled and the reason will be appended to its notes for the audit trail. Bikes attached to this order are not changed.
paintOrderDetail.cancelReasonPlaceholder: e.g. Painter shut down for the holiday — re-batched next week.
paintOrderDetail.bikesDescEdit: The frames that physically ship with this batch — a bike here is blocked from building while the order is out. What gets painted (and the pricing) lives on the items above.
paintOrderDetail.bikesAttached: {count, plural, one {1 bike attached.} other {# bikes attached.}}
paintOrderDetail.addBikeDesc: The bike ships with this batch and is blocked from building while the order is out. Bikes already in an open order are not shown. What gets painted is set on the item lines.
paintOrderDetail.addBikeNotesPlaceholder: Optional — anything specific to this bike.
paintOrderDetail.itemsDescEdit: What gets painted, and how many. Prices follow the supplier's current list (qty tiers count per part type across the order) and freeze when the order is sent.
paintOrderDetail.itemsDescSent: Cost basis frozen when the order was sent — a new price list never rewrites it.
paintOrderDetail.noItemsEdit: No items yet — add what gets painted. The order can't be sent without items.
paintOrderDetail.unpricedWarning: {count, plural, one {1 line has no price on the current list — sending is blocked until priced.} other {# lines have no price on the current list — sending is blocked until priced.}}
paintOrderDetail.noPriceListWarning: This supplier has no current price list for this service — items can't be priced or sent.
paintOrderDetail.addItemDesc: A part type × quantity (× colour). The price resolves from the supplier's current list — qty tiers count the part type's total across the whole order.
paintOrderDetail.sharedTierHint: Two lines of the same part in different colours share one qty tier.
paintOrderDetail.itemNotesPlaceholder: Optional — anything specific to these pieces.
paintOrderDetail.errQtyWhole: Quantity must be a whole number above zero.

invoices.title: Invoices
invoices.subtitle: Uninvoiced work first — then everything already drafted or issued.
invoices.woSectionDesc: Completed, billable, not yet on an invoice. Value is parts at retail plus labor, minus what the customer's agreement covers.
invoices.woEmpty: Nothing waiting — completed billable work orders land here.
invoices.soSectionDesc: Delivered with no invoice yet. Lines copy from the SO; frame numbers of the delivered bikes land in the descriptions.
invoices.soEmpty: No delivered sales orders are waiting for an invoice.
invoices.feeSectionDesc: Billed in arrears, one invoice per customer, one line per agreement-month. Partial months are pro-rated by days.
invoices.feeEmpty: No active service agreements carry a monthly fee.
invoices.emptyDesc: Create the first one from a completed work order above.

invoiceDetail.linesDescDeposit: Deposit draft — issuing assigns the invoice number and locks these lines.
invoiceDetail.linesDescFinal: Final draft — issuing assigns the invoice number and locks these lines.
invoiceDetail.linesDescDraft: Draft — issuing assigns the invoice number and locks these lines.
invoiceDetail.notesDesc: Internal — not printed on the invoice.
invoiceDetail.issueWarning: Issuing assigns the next sequential invoice number and locks the invoice — it can't be edited or cancelled afterwards.
invoiceDetail.economicNoTokens: e-conomic tokens are not set — add ECONOMIC_APP_SECRET_TOKEN and ECONOMIC_AGREEMENT_GRANT_TOKEN to .env.local (and Vercel).

serviceAgreements.title: Service agreements
serviceAgreements.subtitle: Coverage agreements per customer or unit. Drives work-order coverage and the map's renewal layer.
serviceAgreements.emptyDesc: Coverage agreements drive work-order billing and the map's renewal layer.

serviceAgreementDetail.bikesDescUnit: In-service bikes owned by this unit.
serviceAgreementDetail.bikesDescOrg: In-service bikes owned by this organisation.
serviceAgreementDetail.bikesEmptyUnit: No in-service bikes are currently owned by this unit.
serviceAgreementDetail.bikesEmptyOrg: No in-service bikes are currently owned by this organisation.
serviceAgreementDetail.coveredWosDesc: Work orders this agreement has covered.

serviceAgreementForm.newSubtitle: Record a coverage agreement for a customer (or one of their units).
serviceAgreementForm.sectionScopeDesc: Pick the customer. Optionally narrow the agreement to one of their units (e.g. a kommune department) — otherwise it covers the whole organisation.
serviceAgreementForm.sectionCoverageDesc: What the agreement covers, and the recurring fee. Tiered per-bike pricing comes later — this is a single monthly fee for now.
serviceAgreementForm.coverageHint: A work order on a covered bike is non-billable only when both parts and labour are covered.
serviceAgreementForm.sectionNotesDesc: Internal — not shown to the customer.

customers.title: Customers
customers.emptyDesc: Add your first customer to start assigning bikes and tracking service.

customerDetail.archivedBanner: This customer is archived. Bikes still pointed here keep that link for historical reference.
customerDetail.archiveDesc: The customer will be hidden from the list. Any bikes still pointed at this customer keep that link so historical assignments remain visible.
customerDetail.archiveReasonHint: If given, this is appended to the customer notes for the audit trail.

assignedBikes.title: Assigned bikes
assignedBikes.emptyDesc: Once bikes are assigned to this customer, they appear here.

contacts.title: Contacts
contacts.dialogDesc: At least a name or email is required so the entry is identifiable.
contacts.emptyDesc: Add the people you talk to at this customer — facilities, reception, billing.

units.title: Sub-units
units.dialogDesc: Sub-units are departments, sites, or wings within the customer that bikes can be assigned to.
units.emptyDesc: Add departments, sites, or wings if bikes need to be assigned more granularly than the whole customer.
units.addressPlaceholder: Optional — if different from the main customer address.

customerForm.newSubtitle: Capture the basics now — billing and contact details can be filled in later from the edit screen.
customerForm.secIdentificationDesc: The legal name is what appears on invoices. Display names are friendlier labels we can show on documents and the customer detail page.
customerForm.secTaxDesc: Identifiers used on Danish invoicing and EAN-based public-sector billing.
customerForm.secContactDesc: Primary point of contact. Used for service updates and invoices.
customerForm.secAddressDesc: Where bikes get delivered and invoices land. Public sector usually uses EAN billing anyway, but a fallback postal address is useful.
customerForm.secBillingDesc: Currency the customer is invoiced in. Payment terms default to net 30 — adjust per contract.
customerForm.secNotesDesc: Internal notes about this customer — not shown to them.

customerMap.title: Map
customerMap.emptyDesc: Customers, prospects, and bikes appear here once they have a location. Add a postal address (or assign a bike) and it shows up.
customerMap.noPinsMatch: No pins match the current view / segment.

adminHome.heading: Admin
adminHome.subtitle: Controlled-vocab lists and app-wide defaults. Edits here flow into new PO lines; existing snapshots stay frozen.
adminHome.categoriesDesc: The hierarchy parts are classified under. Every part carries one.
adminHome.categoriesStat: {count, plural, one {# active category} other {# active categories}}
adminHome.coloursDesc: Bike colours and finishes. Edits flow into new pickers; existing records keep their reference.
adminHome.coloursStat: {count, plural, one {# active colour} other {# active colours}}
adminHome.familiesDesc: Product families that group bike templates (e.g. Norma over its sizes) on the templates list.
adminHome.familiesStat: {count, plural, one {# active family} other {# active families}}
adminHome.kitsDesc: Colour + number sticker labels for part boxes — the assembly floor picks complete part sets by code.
adminHome.kitsStat: {count, plural, one {# active kit} other {# active kits}}
adminHome.locationsDesc: Physical sites stock lives at. The primary location is the default for receiving and consumption.
adminHome.locationsStat: {count, plural, one {# active location} other {# active locations}}
adminHome.suppliersDesc: Vendors parts are bought from. Used by part offerings, purchase orders, and paint orders.
adminHome.suppliersStat: {count, plural, one {# active supplier} other {# active suppliers}}
adminHome.hsCodesDesc: Classify parts so EU import duty rolls into the landed cost.
adminHome.hsCodesStat: {count, plural, one {# active code} other {# active codes}}
adminHome.fxRatesDesc: Currency-to-DKK conversion rates from ECB via Frankfurter.
adminHome.servicesDesc: Supplier-issued tiered prices for outsourced work (painting). A change is a new revision; sent orders stay frozen.
adminHome.servicesStat: {count, plural, one {# current list} other {# current lists}}
adminHome.segmentsDesc: Hotel / hospital / municipality / FM / B2B / B2C. Used to classify organisations and report on the customer mix.
adminHome.segmentsStat: {count, plural, one {# active segment} other {# active segments}}
adminHome.mapDesc: Geocoded view of customers and prospects — a sales and routing aid.
adminHome.settingsDesc: App-wide defaults (transport %, primary location, hide location info).

adminFx.heading: FX rates
adminFx.subtitle: Currency conversion rates against DKK. PO lines snapshot the rate for their order date at insert — historical lines are not touched unless you run the backfill below.
adminFx.latestDesc: One row per currency pair, showing the most recent rate stored.
adminFx.emptyState: No FX rates on file. Click “Refresh latest rates” to pull from Frankfurter.
adminFx.actionsDesc: Manual triggers. The same refresh runs automatically every day at 17:00 UTC via Vercel Cron (see /api/cron/refresh-fx-rates).
adminFx.attribution: Rates come from <link>frankfurter.app</link> (ECB reference rates, same data Danmarks Nationalbank publishes as the daily fixing). Free, no API key, history to 1999. Backfill walks every non-DKK PO line, looks up the rate for its order date, and updates the snapshot — inventory_movements unit cost is recomputed too.

adminFamilies.heading: Families
adminFamilies.subtitle: Product families group bike templates on the templates list (e.g. “Norma” over its sizes). Order them with the sort field; archived families drop out of the template picker but keep their existing templates grouped.
adminFamilies.emptyState: No families yet. Add one to start grouping templates.
adminFamilies.editSubtitle: Edit the family, reorder it, or archive it.
adminFamilies.newSubtitle: Add a product family, then pick it on the template form.
adminFamilies.nameHint: Groups this family’s templates together on the templates list.
adminFamilies.activeLabel: Active (shown in the template family picker)

adminCategories.archiveDescription: Archiving hides this category from new-part pickers and the parts filter. Existing parts keep their classification.
adminCategories.description: The hierarchy parts are classified under. Every part carries one category. Archiving hides a category from new-part pickers and the parts filter while leaving existing parts classified.
adminCategories.descriptionEnPlaceholder: Optional — what belongs in this category.
adminCategories.emptyState: No categories yet. Add one to start classifying parts.
adminCategories.hintChildren: {count, plural, one {# sub-category stays visible} other {# sub-categories stay visible}}
adminCategories.hintParts: {count, plural, one {# part references this category} other {# parts reference this category}}
adminCategories.newDescription: Pick a parent to nest it, or leave it top-level. The category is immediately selectable on new parts.
adminCategories.noPartsYet: No parts are classified directly under this category yet.
adminCategories.parentHint: Leave as top level for a main category, or nest it under an existing one.
adminCategories.restoreDescription: Restoring makes this category selectable again for new parts.
adminCategories.sortHint: Lower numbers sort first within the same level; ties fall back to alphabetical.
adminCategories.title: Part categories

adminColors.archiveNoUsage: Archiving hides this colour from new bike + MO pickers. No records reference it currently.
adminColors.archiveWithUsage: {count, plural, one {# bike / MO references this colour. Archiving hides it from new pickers; existing records keep their reference.} other {# bikes / MOs reference this colour. Archiving hides it from new pickers; existing records keep their reference.}}
adminColors.coatingHint: Optional. Make “matte” and “glossy” of the same RAL separate colours so the finish carries through to the build and paint order.
adminColors.coatingsDescription: The finishes offered when classifying a colour (e.g. matte RAL 9005). Archived finishes drop out of the picker but stay on existing colours.
adminColors.emptyState: No colours yet. Add one to start.
adminColors.hexHint: Optional. Used for the colour chip throughout the app.
adminColors.newDescription: Add a colour to the palette. Bike + MO pickers default to showing active colours.
adminColors.pageDescription: The colour palette bikes can ship in. Bike + MO pickers default to showing active colours; existing records that reference an archived colour keep their reference.
adminColors.ralConflict: Hex doesn’t match RAL {code} ({hex}). The painter mixes to RAL — the on-screen chip won’t match.
adminColors.ralHint: Optional. For the painter (Metacoat) to mix consistently. A known RAL sets the colour (auto-fills the hex).
adminColors.ralUnknown: “{code}” isn’t a recognised RAL Classic code — no colour to show. Check for a typo, or set the hex manually if it’s a non-Classic RAL.
adminColors.restoreHint: Restoring makes this colour selectable again in new pickers.
adminColors.slugHint: Stable identifier used in URLs / API. Leave blank to auto-derive.
adminColors.sortHint: Lower numbers appear first in pickers.

adminHsCodes.antiDumpingError: Anti-dumping must be a number between 0 and 200, or blank.
adminHsCodes.antiDumpingHint: Optional second tariff column applied alongside the base duty for goods subject to EU anti-dumping measures (most Chinese-origin bicycle parts under heading 8714 carry <mono>48.5</mono> %). Snapshotted onto PO lines and added to the landed-cost formula.
adminHsCodes.archiveNoUsage: Archiving hides this code from new part pickers. No parts reference it currently.
adminHsCodes.archiveWithUsage: {count, plural, one {# part references this code} other {# parts reference this code}}. Archiving hides it from new part pickers; existing PO lines keep their snapshotted tariff so nothing downstream breaks.
adminHsCodes.emptyState: No HS codes yet. Add one to start classifying parts.
adminHsCodes.newDescription: Tariff is snapshotted onto each new PO line at insert. Editing this code later doesn't retroactively change cost basis.
adminHsCodes.noPartsYet: No parts are classified under this code yet. Assign it on a part's edit page.
adminHsCodes.notesPlaceholder: Optional — e.g. footnote on rate of return.
adminHsCodes.pageDescription: EU import duty classifications. Each part can carry one; PO lines snapshot the tariff at insert so future edits don't retroactively change cost basis. Codes with parts attached can be archived but not deleted.
adminHsCodes.restoreHint: Restoring makes this code selectable again in new parts.
adminHsCodes.tariffError: Tariff must be a number between 0 and 100.
adminHsCodes.tariffHint: EU import duty as a percent — e.g. <mono>5</mono> for 5 %, <mono>10.2</mono> for 10.2 %. Snapshotted onto each new PO line at insert.

adminKits.archiveDescription: Archiving hides the kit from pickers, pick lists, and the parts filter. The {count, plural, one {# labelled part} other {# labelled parts}} keep the label (greyed) until removed.
adminKits.editKitDescription: Changing colour or number changes the sticker code — reprint labels afterwards.
adminKits.empty: No kits yet — create the first sticker label.
adminKits.labelledPartsDescription: Parts carrying this sticker. Tag and untag from each part's detail page, or in bulk from a bike template's BOM.
adminKits.newKitSubtitle: The sticker identity is the colour plus an optional number — "Red" on its own, or "Red 1". The floor picks by the full code, so it prints big on the label.
adminKits.restoreDescription: Restoring puts the kit back in pickers and pick lists.
adminKits.stickerSheetHint: {count, plural, one {# part sticker} other {# part stickers}} + 1 kit header sticker. Print on A4 label paper and cut along the borders.
adminKits.subtitle: Colour + number sticker labels ("Red 1") for part boxes, so the assembly floor picks complete part sets per build.
adminKits.title: Kits

adminLocations.archiveNoMovements: Archiving hides this location from new pickers. No movements reference it currently.
adminLocations.archiveWithMovements: {count, plural, one {# movement references this location. Archiving hides it from new pickers; the ledger keeps its history.} other {# movements reference this location. Archiving hides it from new pickers; the ledger keeps its history.}}
adminLocations.blockedPrimaryDesc: This is the primary shop location. Set a different primary in Settings before archiving it.
adminLocations.codeHint: Short stable identifier shown on movements and receiving.
adminLocations.emptyState: No locations yet. Add one to start.
adminLocations.heading: Locations
adminLocations.newSubtitle: Add a physical site stock can live at. Set it as the primary location in Settings if it should be the default for receiving and consumption.
adminLocations.restoreDesc: Restoring makes this location selectable again in new pickers.
adminLocations.subtitle: The physical sites stock lives at. Most shops run one. The primary location is where parts are received into and consumed from by default — mark it on its row below.
adminLocations.visibilityHiddenDesc: Stock shows a single total, the movements ledger drops its location column, and receiving / stock-adjust target the primary location.
adminLocations.visibilityShownDesc: Per-location stock, the movements location column, and the receive / stock-adjust pickers are all visible.
adminLocations.visibilityTitleHidden: Location detail is hidden across the app
adminLocations.visibilityTitleShown: Location detail is shown across the app

adminSegments.archiveDescriptionNone: Archiving hides this segment from new pickers. No organisations reference it currently.
adminSegments.archiveDescriptionUsed: {count, plural, one {# organisation uses this segment.} other {# organisations use this segment.}} Archiving hides it from new pickers; existing organisations keep their reference.
adminSegments.description: Classification for organisations (hotel, hospital, municipality, etc.). Edits flow into new pickers; existing organisations keep their reference even if the segment is later archived.
adminSegments.descriptionEnPlaceholder: Optional. Shown as helper text in pickers.
adminSegments.emptyState: No segments yet. Add one to start.
adminSegments.newDescription: Add a new classification for organisations. Used by pickers on the organization form and downstream reporting.
adminSegments.restoreDescription: Restoring makes this segment selectable again in new pickers.
adminSegments.slugHint: Stable identifier. Leave blank to auto-derive.
adminSegments.sortHint: Lower numbers appear first in pickers.
adminSegments.title: Customer segments

adminServices.emptyState: No price lists yet — add the first supplier list to price service orders.
adminServices.everyPartTypeHasRow: Every part type has a row.
adminServices.newPriceListSubtitle: The supplier's first list for a service. Fill in the prices you have; blank cells simply stay unpriced.
adminServices.newRevisionSubtitle: Starts from {name} (v{version}). Adjust the numbers, review the diff, publish — the old revision archives and sent orders keep their frozen prices.
adminServices.noChangesYet: No changes yet — identical to the current revision.
adminServices.priceError: Prices must be numbers of zero or above.
adminServices.pricesDescription: One row per part type, one column per quantity tier. Blank cells stay unpriced; the supplier's own item number sits under each price.
adminServices.subtitle: Supplier-issued per-piece prices for outsourced work (painting today), in quantity tiers. A change is a new revision — sent orders keep the prices frozen on them.
adminServices.title: Service price lists

adminSettings.accountingDescription: Issued invoices push to e-conomic as draft journal vouchers — the bookkeeper reviews and books them there. API tokens live in env vars; this card holds the agreement numbers. Confirm the journal and revenue account with the revisor before the first real push.
adminSettings.appLanguageHelp: The language for the office / admin side of the app.
adminSettings.communicationDescription: Sender identity for app-generated email (PO to supplier; the phone-call pipeline later) and the workshop phone. Test mode reroutes all mail to the test inboxes.
adminSettings.dnsDescription: Reference copy of the DNS records the email provider needs for domain verification. The records take effect at the DNS host — keep the values and their status here so they're never buried in a dashboard or an email thread.
adminSettings.dnsEmpty: No DNS records on file yet. Add the rows from the email provider's domain-verification page.
adminSettings.economicEnableLabel: Enable the e-conomic integration (shows the push button on issued invoices)
adminSettings.economicTokensMissing: API tokens are not set. Add ECONOMIC_APP_SECRET_TOKEN and ECONOMIC_AGREEMENT_GRANT_TOKEN to .env.local (and Vercel), then restart — tokens are secrets and never live in this form.
adminSettings.fromAddressHelp: Sender for app-generated email. Must be on the domain the email provider has verified.
adminSettings.languageDescription: Working language for the office app and the workshop floor. Defaults to English.
adminSettings.languageRolloutNote: These save your preference now. The interface is still being translated, so some screens stay in English until that rolls out — customer-facing documents (invoices, the public report) already follow their own language.
adminSettings.purchasingDescription: Default values pre-filled into new PO line dialogs.
adminSettings.recordValuePlaceholder: Record value — paste from the provider
adminSettings.replyToHelp: Where supplier replies land — usually the real inbox.
adminSettings.sendingDomainHelp: The domain outbound email sends from. The records below are what the email provider asks you to add at the DNS host — they take effect there, not here; this list is the paste-source and status tracker.
adminSettings.subtitle: App-wide defaults read at form load. Snapshots already written to PO lines or HS codes are not touched.
adminSettings.testModeHelp: While on, every email the app sends goes to the test recipients below instead of the real recipient (the mail says who it was meant for). Untick to go live.
adminSettings.testModeToggle: Test mode — reroute all outbound email
adminSettings.title: Settings
adminSettings.transportError: Transport % must be a number between 0 and 100.
adminSettings.transportHelpSuffix: for 10.2 %. New PO lines pre-fill this; existing lines keep their own snapshot.
adminSettings.workerLanguageHelp: The language the build floor and ticket / work-order screens use. Becomes a per-worker setting later.
adminSettings.workshopPhoneHelp: Shown on outbound documents; the phone-call → ticket pipeline will use it for call routing and SMS later.
adminSettings.reportUrlDesc: Share this URL with customers who need to report a bike issue. They’ll scan the QR sticker or enter the frame number; no login required.
adminSettings.reportUrlFallback: The “I don’t know my bike” fallback lives at {helpUrl} — useful when a customer can’t find the QR sticker. Both paths land in /maintenance/tickets; unidentified-bike reports show up flagged “Needs triage” in the Bike column.
